hypothesis: If the claim holds, many more European-native plant species are naturalised in La Plata and Australia than southern-hemisphere-native species are naturalised in Europe.
pass_criterion: Ratio of the number of European-native species naturalised in Argentina/Uruguay or Australia to the number of southern-hemisphere-native species naturalised in any European region is >= 10.
interpretation: 'Naturalised' follows GloNAF status classes. 'Southern forms' means species whose native range lies mainly in the southern hemisphere, which requires native-range information from an external source such as POWO joined to GloNAF. 'Cover the ground' and 'beaten the natives' are not measured; only counts of naturalised species are.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF)
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides lists of naturalised alien plant taxa per region (country, state, island) including Argentina, Uruguay, Australia and European countries, allowing counts of naturalised taxa by region.
